title: Three-way membership split proves a cut yields valid triangles (IMO 2026 Q4)
intent: Prove that an admissible cut of a valid triangle yields two valid triangles by unfolding the positivity conjunct ∀ y ∈ {a, b, c}, 0 < y of IsTriangle into a three-way disjunction via mem_triple, then splitting each of the two resulting membership hypotheses with rcases hy with h | h | h so every branch closes from the cut's interval bounds.

parent.name: cut_preserves
parent.statement: theorem cut_preserves {s L R : Multiset ℝ} (hs : IsTriangle s) (hcut : IsCut s L R) : IsTriangle L ∧ IsTriangle R

children.name: L: y = β
children.statement: 0 < y under h : y = β (first branch of rcases on y ∈ {β, x, 180 - β - x})

children.name: L: y = x
children.statement: 0 < y under h : y = x (second branch; linarith from γ < x and 0 < γ)

children.name: L: y = 180 - β - x
children.statement: 0 < y under h : y = 180 - β - x (third branch; linarith from x < 180 - β)

children.name: R: y = γ
children.statement: 0 < y under h : y = γ (first branch of rcases on y ∈ {γ, 180 - x, x - γ})

children.name: R: y = 180 - x
children.statement: 0 < y under h : y = 180 - x (second branch; linarith from x < 180 - β and 0 < β)

children.name: R: y = x - γ
children.statement: 0 < y under h : y = x - γ (third branch; linarith from γ < x)

applicability.goal_shape: A conjunct of the form ∀ y ∈ {a, b, c}, P y over a small fixed multiset, where membership is rewritten by an iff-lemma to y = a ∨ y = b ∨ y = c and split with rcases h with h | h | h. Here IsTriangle is s.card = 3 ∧ (∀ x ∈ s, 0 < x) ∧ s.sum = 180, and the split is applied to the positivity conjunct of IsTriangle L and IsTriangle R after unfolding L = {β, x, 180 - β - x} and R = {γ, 180 - x, x - γ}.
applicability.use_when: the multiset is small and fixed (three elements), membership unfolds to a finite disjunction via an iff-lemma, and each element's property is already available as a hypothesis or follows by linarith from interval hypotheses in scope (here γ < x and x < 180 - β from IsCut).
applicability.avoid_when: the multiset is large, unbounded, or described only by a general predicate (the split becomes huge or impossible); the disjunction y = a ∨ ... ∨ y = c needs its own proof (state that as a separate child); or the branches need different, non-computational arguments so a uniform rcases does not close them.

claims.claim: The parent cut_preserves closes from its children: constructor yields IsTriangle L and IsTriangle R; each refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩ yields the card, positivity and sum conjuncts, closed by card_triple, sum_triple + ring, and rcases hy with h | h | h (three branches, two by linarith and one by exact hβ/exact hγ) respectively.

consequences: Creates one goal per element of the multiset (six in total: three for L, three for R). Exhaustiveness is free only because mem_triple is an iff that already unfolds membership to the full three-way disjunction; without such a lemma the writer must first prove y = a ∨ y = b ∨ y = c. Each branch must substitute the element it landed on (rw [h]) before the known bounds apply. The linarith branches rely on the cut's interval hypotheses γ < x and x < 180 - β (destructured from IsCut at line 65) together with the positivity hβ/hγ; if any of these is not in scope the branch will not close.
